model_reported.summary: Compared prior official trial means as context, treated the seven distinct programs as evidence against a simple rerun, and made no speed claim before controller correctness and timing.

memory_lessons.applicability: CTA source tiling with one target per thread; compare tile sizes under the same official protocol.
memory_lessons.claim: The compact 128-thread trial was faster than the compact 192-thread trial in the supplied measurements, but this does not establish the best tile size or explain the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a distinct intermediate 160-thread CTA/tile after correctness passes.

proposal.hypothesis: Test an intermediate 160-thread CTA/source tile with compact 16-byte shared source records. Prior measurements found the compact 128-thread version valid at 0.00089008 s and the compact 192-thread version valid at 0.00092263 s; the 96-thread version was slower at 0.00098055 s. With seven distinct prior programs and no repeats, this five-warp configuration tests whether fewer source-tile iterations than at 128 threads can offset a larger CTA and 2,560-byte shared allocation. No speedup is assumed.

retained: Set block and items_per_block to 160, maintaining exactly one target per thread and a matching 160-source CTA tile.
Stage only source position and mass in a dynamic shared array of compact records, using 2,560 bytes.
Retain ascending source interaction order, barriers around each staged tile, partial-tile bounds, and guards for target reads and output writes.
